subject: low densities/abundances and using gdistsamp vs. distsamp

messages.author: d3fd439c2e48caf1
messages.subject: low densities/abundances and using gdistsamp vs. distsamp
parts:
Hello esteemed unmarked-makers and users,

I'm assisting some colleagues who have collected repeated distance-sampling data for several bird species along a number of transects. Based on their experience in the field and previous research, it appears that densities are very low and detections are rarely more than 2 (and often 1) individuals per species/transect. 

I'd like to advise/assist them in the use of gdistsamp given they have repeat surveys, distance information, survey-level covariates, and site-level covariates, however... 

There are two major issues I see with their data, so I'd appreciate your suggestions on approaches (e.g. gdistsampl vs. distsamp vs. ???)
1) there are only 2 visits per transect
2) "true" abundances appear quite low (many 0 and 1 detections) and aren't likely to be neg bin or Poisson distributed (closer to presence/absence than abundance). 

Forgive me if this has been covered before and thanks (as always) for the ongoing development of unmarked.

Giancarlo

messages.author: 681fb59733e01a1e
messages.subject: Re: [unmarked] low densities/abundances and using gdistsamp vs. distsamp
parts:
Giancarlo,
 gdistsamp() is the correct function for modeling repeated distance sampling data.
 I suspect with such low counts per transect, the Poisson abundance model will fit well, you should not have any problems there.
 The total sample size will affect how complex your models are, of course, so be careful there.
regards
andy

Thanks Andy for the quick and informative reply! 

Just a quick follow-up: my colleagues have a number of species with varying abundances/densities/detections and I'm concerned some will have inadequate presences/counts for modeling.  In the occupancy modeling framework, I've adhered to using only species with ~20%-80% naive site occupancy (either this is in the book or I heard it from Darryl); is there a comparable 'rule-of-thumb' for these gdistsamp models?

Thanks again,

Giancarlo
